Problem: Missing GPIO_AF7_USART3
Context: repo=stm32c0xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=UART, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=8
Root cause: Hello @rum-htkw, Thank you for your report, it seems that point makes sense and will be tracked internally.
Fix: When creating a project with CubeMX and the STM32C092RCTx and want to put USART3_TX on PC14, CubeMX will generate a project which can't be compiled.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, UART, bug_report, medium, bug, internal bug tracker, gpio, USART3_TX, PC14, GPIO_AF7_USART3

Technical details:
When creating a project with CubeMX and the STM32C092RCTx and want to put USART3_TX on PC14, CubeMX will generate a project which can't be compiled. The issue is that the definition of GPIO_AF7_USART3 is missing in stm32c0xx_hal_gpio_ex.h. I have created a pull request which solves the issue: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32c0xx-hal-driver/pull/7

Hello @rum-htkw, Thank you for your report, it seems that point makes sense and will be tracked internally. I'll keep you informed about last update. KIWA Mohamed Chaker. ST Internal Reference: c36458ecf9b8c31c580b5e13ea29a5f7

Problem: register keyword incompatible with C++17
Context: repo=stm32c0xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=ADC, layer=LL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=high, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=5
Root cause: Hi @pataelmo, Thank you for your report.
Fix: There were similar issues found and fixed for the H7 and F4 code bases, but wanted to raise this simple fix for preventing future compiler issues for everyone.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: LL, ADC, bug_report, high, bug, internal bug tracker, spotted before customer, hal

Technical details:
There were similar issues found and fixed for the H7 and F4 code bases, but wanted to raise this simple fix for preventing future compiler issues for everyone. https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/issues/15 https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF4/issues/27 The issue is that the register keyword was depreciated in C++11 and removed in C++17 because the intent of the keyword no longer makes sense with modern compilers capabilities. Specific changes need, remove register keyword on the following lines (potentially more, but this is what my compiler hit as definite errors): stm32c0xx_ll_adc.h:4010 stm32c0xx_ll_adc.h:4115 stm32c0xx_ll_adc.h:4120 stm32c0xx_ll_rtc.h:1077 stm32c0xx_ll_rtc.h:1105 stm32c0xx_ll_rtc.h:1410 stm32c0xx_ll_rtc.h:1438 stm32c0xx_ll_rtc.h:1741

Key comments:
Hi @pataelmo, Thank you for your report. I'll log an internal tracker. BR, Mohamed Chaker. ST Internal Reference: 222353 ST Internal Reference: 222355 The LL RTC issue has been fixed in commit a7d5b22edf256a15fd58621b514b54b40967070f The LL ADC issue has been fixed in commit 6ea9e856e09f46557c18ca376eeebfd0c9ee6363

issues.issue_title: Incorrect Alternate Function Mapping for FDCAN
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: Incorrect Alternate Function Mapping for FDCAN
Context: repo=stm32c0xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=CAN, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=3
Root cause: Hello @promed-jmjablonski, Thank you for this heads-up.
Fix: When testing the FDCAN on the STM32C092FCP6 with PB8 (Rx) and PC14 (Tx), we discovered that the alternate function mapping in the stm32c0xx_hal_gpio_ex.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, CAN, bug_report, medium, bug, internal bug tracker, gpio, FDCAN, STM32C092FCP6, PB8, PC14, DS14720

Technical details:
When testing the FDCAN on the STM32C092FCP6 with PB8 (Rx) and PC14 (Tx), we discovered that the alternate function mapping in the stm32c0xx_hal_gpio_ex.h definitions is incorrect. According to DS14720 Rev. 2, the alternate function mapping for PC14 should be AF13. However, in the definitions, AF13 is assigned to TIM3 and TIM14. Additionally, in STM32CubeIDE (v1.19) the code generator selected AF15 for PC14 in the stm32c0xx_hal_msp.c file, which is used for EVENTOUT.

Key comments:
Hello @promed-jmjablonski, Thank you for this heads-up. Let's have this fixed. ST Internal Reference: 219065 Fixed in Commit: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32c0xx-hal-driver/commit/18bb669c40be6841b302b8a756b3cb004d0c1769

Problem: Clarification about DMAMUX tim14_trgo
Context: repo=stm32c0xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=DMA, layer=LL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=low, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=2
Root cause: ST Internal Reference: 205085 Hello @znuh, Thank you for your contribution.
Fix: I'm not sure if this is a bug, but I stumbled upon this and it looks a bit odd to me: The C0 RM0490 Rev 5 Table 50/51 list the DMAMUX trigger inputs and synchronization inputs.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: LL, DMA, bug_report, low, bug, documentation, internal bug tracker, hal, dmamux, RM0490, AN5969, RM0444

Technical details:
I'm not sure if this is a bug, but I stumbled upon this and it looks a bit odd to me: The C0 RM0490 Rev 5 Table 50/51 list the DMAMUX trigger inputs and synchronization inputs. In Table 50 (assignment of trigger inputs to resources) _tim14_trgo_ is assigned to Trigger Input **22**, whereas in Table 51 (assignment of synchronization inputs to resources) it is assigned to Sync Input **21**. All other mappings are consistent between trigger inputs and synchronization inputs. Therefore I'm wondering, if the _tim14_trgo_ entry in Table 51 might be wrong. (Should it be assigned to **22**?) AN5969 section 5.16 says: > When the same peripherals are available on both products, their DMA assignment of multiplexer inputs to resources, trigger inputs to resources, and synchronization inputs to resources are identical. But in the G0 series (RM0444 Rev 6) _TIM14_OC_ is mapped to Input **22** both for Trigger and Sync Input. So, the AN5969 section 5.16 statement would be wrong, if on the C0 family _tim14_trgo_ really is mapped to synchronization input 21. I also checked the definition here in the HAL: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32c0xx-hal-driver/blob/main/Inc/stm32c0xx_ll_dmamux.h#L250 This definition is **21** in accordance with RM0490. So, if the RM is wrong about the _tim14_trgo_ sync assignment, the HAL definition would also be wrong. Could you check, if the _tim14_trgo_ assignment in RM0490 really is correct? (I did not encounter this by debugging a firmware. I read RM0490 for an opensource firmware library and it just seemed odd.)

Key comments:
ST Internal Reference: 205085 Hello @znuh, Thank you for your contribution. We confirm that there is an error in the reference manual. We will correct this discrepancy in the next publication of the reference manual RM0490. Additionally, we will update our drivers to ensure they align with the corrected documentation. ST Internal Reference: 205214 Thank you for checking & confirming! I'm not sure if you prefer leaving this issue open for now or close it. Feel free to close it if you want, or let me know when I shall close it. Fixed in ae48b633b91414436f150f699472a30ddd1ac4af
